definition: The football class means every real physical football visible in the frame: the active match ball, spare balls, ball-boy balls, balls behind the goal, sideline balls, and any other real visible football.

active_vs_non_active.rationale: The detector answers 'is this a football'. Which football the play is centred on is a temporal question that a single frame cannot answer reliably, so it belongs to the downstream selector, which can use motion and continuity that a frame-level detector does not have.

consequences.note: The 22 existing annotations a human marked EXISTING_NON_ACTIVE_BALL_GT are CORRECT under this policy. That flag is provenance, never a deletion instruction. Removing an annotation merely for being non-active is forbidden.

flags_that_remain_defect_reports.SUSPECT_FALSE_BALL_GT: not a football at all; still a defect under this policy
flags_that_remain_defect_reports.SUSPECT_BAD_BALL_BOX: a real football whose geometry is wrong; still a defect

forbidden_without_a_new_recorded_decisio: treating EXISTING_NON_ACTIVE_BALL_GT as a removal instruction
filtering the football class down to the active match ball
dropping NON_ACTIVE_EXTRA_BALL findings when building a corrected export

evidence.why: 22 existing annotations are spare or ball-boy balls, so the source is not ACTIVE_ONLY; 103 other visible spares were left unannotated, so it is not ALL_VISIBLE either. The source applied no consistent rule, which is why this policy has to be stated rather than inferred.
evidence.note: Both rates describe the same 300 images. Under this policy the binding figure is the 28.0% any-visible rate, because every one of those 84 images is missing something the detector is now required to find.

does_not_rewrite_history: Historical decisions stay exactly as recorded. ACTIVE_MATCH_BALL and NON_ACTIVE_EXTRA_BALL classifications remain in the log with their original meaning; this policy governs how they are USED, not what they said.
